learning: If line_loss_events fall and max_error drops below 0.06 but the robot still stalls or leaves at the edge, the next step is more kp or a higher kd. If steering_oscillation rises sharply, reduce kp to about 1.5 before changing geometry. If progress is good but completion time is over 3 s, raise base_speed in steps of 0.1 only while max_error stays under 0.05.
notes: Widened-spread geometry from the Builder with a higher-gain, slower controller matched to the new sensor spacing. Lower speed gives time to recover from drift, which is the failure seen in all 60 baseline trials.
rationale: The race evidence (entityR2B) shows all 60 trials across the three development tracks ended off_track, with zero completions. Mean max_error is 0.062 to 0.064 m, at the 0.06 m limit, and line_loss_events is 1 to 2 per run. The robot is drifting out and not correcting in time. The Builder's proposal (entity0) widens the sensor spread to x = -0.03 to +0.03 m, which keeps the same five sensors, 12 mm footprints and y = 0.05 lead. I keep the Builder's geometry unchanged so the race tests only one change. For the controller, the old weights [-2,-1,0,1,2] spanned only +/-0.02 m. With the new spread, the same weights give a signal slope about 1/3 smaller per metre of offset (weight = x/0.015 instead of x/0.01). I compensate by raising kp from 1.0 to 2.0, which restores and slightly raises the effective steering gain (about 133 per metre against 100 before). I raise kd from 0.2 to 0.3 to damp the extra gain, and keep ki at 0 to avoid windup on curves. I lower base_speed from 1.5 to 1.2, so the robot has more time to correct when it drifts toward the edge. This costs some speed, so finishing in 3 s is less likely, but the current runs never finish anyway, and the first priority is staying on the line. line_loss stays 'last_direction', since the tape has a single side per bend. Expected result, to be confirmed by the race: fewer line-loss events and a lower max_error, which should raise progress above the current 0.12 to 0.19 range.
